lessons_used: Predictions continue to be consistently too high compared to measured and noise-corrected results.
Sign-in reordering (sign_in, reorder) is helpful, averaging +2.2% after noise correction across 2 tests, with 1 winning test (though 1 test showed no clear effect).
Evidence is still thin for adding new adoption screens (adoption, new_screen) as there is only 1 test.
carried_retests: Compact welcome banner with quick start guide

candidates.title: Spotlight layout for pet generation waiting screen
candidates.change: Redesign the waiting screen using a spotlight layout with progress indicators to show pet generation status clearly.
candidates.why: The waiting step has a long mean duration (2336s) and 3 support emails reported pets not rendering on desktop or app stalling.

guard.reason: Redesigning the waiting screen layout while preserving pet creation status indicators is permitted inside onboarding.

candidates.score_note: Addresses long wait times and pet rendering issues, but requires UI redesign.

candidates.title: Move sign-in after pet generation waiting step
candidates.change: Move sign-in screen after pet generation waiting step so users log in right before entering home_intro.
candidates.why: 8 support emails cited missing or reset pets after re-authenticating; moving sign-in ensures pet generation completes prior to account linking.

guard.reason: Reordering the sign-in step to occur after waiting is explicitly allowed by onboarding reordering rules.

candidates.score_note: Strong support evidence (8 emails) and historical sign-in reorder lift (+2.2%).

candidates.title: Guided photo upload helper sub-flow
candidates.change: Add an extra photo tips screen within the photo upload flow to guide custom pet creation.
candidates.why: 3 support emails reported custom pet creation failing or looking incorrect, contributing to a 39.1% drop-off during adoption.

upload_photos.hint: Follow photo tips to ensure optimal custom pet generation

guard.reason: _order leaves out existing screens ['sign_in']: no step may be removed

candidates.title: Split layout controls center on home intro
candidates.change: Redesign the final home intro screen to a split layout highlighting basic pet controls.
candidates.why: 35.2% drop-off at finish step and 3 support emails reported user confusion on how to control, hide, or talk to the pet after onboarding.

home_welcome.text: Right-click your desktop pet to open controls, hide, or switch modes.

guard.reason: Redesigning the home intro screen layout while maintaining its welcoming function is permitted.

candidates.score_note: Targets high 35.2% finish drop-off, but requires new screen layout.

candidates.title: Account save reassurance copy on path choice
candidates.change: Add body copy reassuring users that created pets will automatically sync to their account.
candidates.why: 8 support messages mentioned concern over reset or missing pets after signing in again.

choose_path.headline: Choose How to Create Your Pet
choose_path.body: Your pet progress is saved safely to your account once created.

guard.reason: Adding progress reassurance copy to the choose path screen is permitted.

candidates.score_note: Low cost copy update backed by 8 support emails regarding pet loss concerns.

candidates.title: Pet trait guidance hint on friend selection
candidates.change: Add a mascot tip component explaining how pet traits influence desktop behavior.
candidates.why: Adoption conversion is low (60.9%) with high decision time (median 89s).

pick_friend.hint: Select traits that match your work habits for the best desktop companion experience.

guard.reason: Asks for personal information and details about the user's work habits.

candidates.title: Desktop permission guidance on waiting screen
candidates.change: Display background status text with system permission hints during pet rendering.
candidates.why: 3 support emails noted app stalling or pet not appearing on desktop.

waiting.hint: If your pet does not appear automatically, check system tray permissions.

guard.reason: Displaying permission hints and time estimates on the waiting screen is permitted.

candidates.score_note: Simple status text guidance targeting desktop rendering stall issues.

candidates.title: Desktop background completion notification
candidates.change: Enable optional desktop notification alert when pet generation completes in background.
candidates.why: Waiting step takes median 201s and mean 2336s, causing users to minimize or forget the app window.

waiting.body: We will notify you on your desktop as soon as your pet is ready to play.

guard.reason: Adding an optional desktop notification setting to the waiting screen is explicitly allowed.

candidates.score_note: Addresses extreme wait times (2336s mean), but requires native feature release.

candidates.title: Compact layout for adoption certificate screen
candidates.change: Change adoption certificate layout to compact view to bring action buttons above fold.
candidates.why: Adoption step has high drop-off (39.1%) and high mean duration (1017s).

guard.reason: Uses promotional 'claim' language associated with gifts or free extras.

candidates.title: Shortcut key hint on home intro screen
candidates.change: Add hint text detailing shortcut keys to show, hide, and interact with desktop pet.
candidates.why: 3 support emails noted post-onboarding confusion regarding hiding and controlling the desktop pet.

home_intro.hint: Use your taskbar or right-click pet menu to quickly show or hide companion.

guard.reason: Adding shortcut key hint text to the home intro screen is allowed inside onboarding.

candidates.score_note: Cheap hint addition to tackle confusion at high drop-off finish step.

lessons_next: Predictions are mostly too high, though they were too low for the finish redesign in round 6 (+1.5% predicted vs +3.1% noise-corrected).
Sign-in reordering (sign_in, reorder) is helpful, averaging +2.2% after noise correction across 2 tests with 1 winning test, though 1 test showed no clear effect.
Evidence is still thin for adding new adoption screens (adoption, new_screen) as there is only 1 test, which showed no clear effect.
Evidence is still thin for finish redesigns (finish, redesign) with only 1 test, despite it winning.
